# K5.3 RMSNorm backward (Triton)

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Class: **Same function** (E1: same function at infinite precision, different floating-point
order)

## 1. Packages

G3, G6 and G6b, where named below, are Firmus's earlier GPT-OSS NVFP4 packages (`nemo_g3_nvfp4_v1`, `nemo_g6_nvfp4_v2`,
`nemo_g6b_nvfp4_v2_1`), withdrawn from this submission and no longer in this repository. Their values, line numbers,
images and test jobs are cited as the record of where evidence was collected ([Index](../KERNELS.md), "Earlier packages").

- `NVFP4_TRITON_RMSNORM_BWD=1` (config line
  148), `NVFP4_RMSNORM_BWD_STAGES=4`
  (line 140). Same values in G3, G6 and G6b and G6c. `NVFP4_RMSNORM_BWD_UNROLL` is not
  set (default 1, patch L1176).
- Code: `transformer_engine/pytorch/ops/basic/nvfp4_triton_rmsnorm_bwd.py`, created by
  `docker/patches/transformer_engine_firmus_nvfp4.patch` L1150–1295 (byte-identical in the three packages);
  installed by `pretrain.py` L49–60 (G3, G6 and G6b: L47–58, same text).
- In this package `NVFP4_RESGRAD=1` (K8.4, `pretrain.py` L108–113) wraps this function again
  (`transformer_engine_firmus_v7.patch` L2267–2282). A call for which a residual or router gradient was handed over
  runs `_rmsnorm_bwd_res_kernel` (L2044–2078): the same per-row arithmetic, with an explicit FMA for dx (L2070–2072)
  and the extra gradient added after the BF16 rounding of dx (L2073–2075); other calls run this item's kernel
  (L2098–2099). K8.4 covers the handed-over sums; the dgamma reduction is this item's `_reduce_rows_kernel` in both
  cases (L2121–2124). The QK RMSNorms of this model are not in this path; their backward is K10.1's.

## 2. What the reference does

TE `27486e03` `tex.rmsnorm_bwd(dz, x, rsigma, gamma, sm_margin, zero_centered_gamma)`, called by
`LayerNormLinear` and by the op fuser's `RMSNorm` op. Per row, with \(\hat x = x\,r\) (\(r\) = rsigma) and
\(g = \gamma\) (or \(\gamma + 1\) when zero-centred):

\[ dx = r\left(dz\,g - \hat x\,\frac{1}{n}\sum_k dz_k g_k \hat x_k\right),\qquad
   d\gamma = \sum_{\text{rows} } dz\,\hat x . \]

TE runs a main kernel and a finalize kernel that reduces dγ (patch docstring L1158–1159: about 240 µs each on
24576 × 2880 BF16). The upstream source is not in the package.

## 3. What this implementation does

1. `pretrain.py` L59–60 replaces `tex.rmsnorm_bwd` and the op module's `rmsnorm_bwd` with the Triton function
   before the CUDA graphs are captured.
2. `rmsnorm_bwd` (patch L1266–1295) launches `2 × (SMs − sm_margin)` persistent programs (L1280). Each program
   takes rows `pid, pid + P, …` (L1216), reads x and dz once, computes dx in FP32 and stores it (`_finish_row`,
   L1191–1198), and accumulates dz·x̂ in an FP32 register vector; at the end it writes one partial row
   (L1242).
3. `_reduce_rows_kernel` (L1245–1260) sums the partials column-wise in FP32 and casts dγ to γ's dtype.
4. `NVFP4_RMSNORM_BWD_STAGES=4` only software-pipelines the row loop (`tl.range(..., num_stages=STAGES)`,
   L1216); the docstring (L1164–1168) states that the stages and unroll options keep the row assignment and the
   summation order.

## 4. Why the result is the same

dx is the same closed-form per-row expression; its row sum `mdot` is evaluated in a different order than TE's, so
dx can differ in the last bit. dγ is the same sum over rows in a different order (per-program partials, then a
column reduction; TE uses its own two-kernel reduction). Class **Same function** (E1).

vs reference (jobs 22434 and 22694, captured layer input and `pre_mlp_layernorm` weight of seven layers of a G6
run, 24576 × 2880): dx differs in 276–341 of 70 781 760 elements (max 0.0078 on seeded real shapes, job 22168),
dγ in 0–3 of 2880. vs FP64: not quoted here (Section 9).

## 5. Numerics

BF16 x, dz; FP32 rsigma, γ promoted to FP32; all arithmetic FP32; dx rounded once to the input dtype; dγ partials
FP32, reduced in FP32, one cast at the end. The dγ summation order depends on the number of programs, i.e. on the
GPU's SM count and `sm_margin` (`NVTE_BWD_LAYERNORM_SM_MARGIN=20`, config
L154); for a fixed GPU and
config it is fixed, so the result is repeatable.

## 6. Shapes and fallbacks

- **Gate:** none. Every call of `tex.rmsnorm_bwd` and of the op module's `rmsnorm_bwd` goes to the Triton function
  (`pretrain.py` L59–60). Non-contiguous `x` or `dz` are copied to contiguous (L1271–1274).
- **Falls back:** never; there is no path back to TE's kernel while the switch is on.
- **Assumes:** (a) the caller's positional signature `(dz, x, rsigma, gamma, sm_margin, zero_centered_gamma)`
  (L1266); a TE version with another signature would fail at the first backward. (b) A row fits one program:
  `BLOCK_N = next_power_of_2(cols)` (L1279), 4096 for 2880; very wide rows would spill registers (slower, same
  result). (c) rsigma is one FP32 value per row, as TE's forward stores it (L1187).
- **Check:** config lines 148 and 140. No log line;
  the replacement is unconditional at import of `pretrain.py`.
  K8.4's install raises if `tex.rmsnorm_bwd` is not this function (`transformer_engine_firmus_v7.patch` L2276–2277), and every `result_*.txt` contains `NVFP4_RESGRAD installed (router 1, fwd 0)` (`result_0.txt` L219), so this item was installed in the scored runs.

## 7. Code

- `transformer_engine_firmus_nvfp4.patch` L1150–1295: `_load_row` L1180–1188, `_finish_row` L1191–1198,
  `_rmsnorm_bwd_kernel` L1201–1242, `_reduce_rows_kernel` L1245–1260, `rmsnorm_bwd` L1266–1295. Applied by
  `Dockerfile` step 4 (`git apply` L113).
- `pretrain.py` L49–60.

## 8. Tests and evidence

Kernel test on the submitted image (Firmus test script `k5_3_k8_4_rmsnorm_bwd.py`, available on request), Triton
vs `tex.rmsnorm_bwd`:

- Job 22884 (this package's image): 67 cases including K8.4 cases, 39 with a difference. The K5.3 cases with a
  difference are real rounding differences: seeded real shapes (351, 367 elements), zero-centred γ (319), 14
  captured layers of this package's training run, job 22873 (285–360), sm_margin 0 and 16 (345, 344), rows 24575 /
  24577 / 24583 (361–362), special values in dz (5804, non-finite propagation) and finite specials in x (45),
  constant rows (69), non-contiguous inputs (63); prefill 0x00 / 0xFF and fresh process give the base case's 351.
  The remaining differing cases are K8.4 cases against TE plus separate adds and the K8.4 fixture.
- Run a vs run b: every digest equal (343 / 0 in job 22434, 50 / 0 in job 22694, 125 / 0 in job 22884).
- Development test `test_triton_rmsnorm_bwd.py` (development repository) loads a development copy.

## 9. Open points

1. vs FP64, unverified here: the Triton and TE errors are recorded as being of the same size, without a job
   number; the error values per output are in the test records (available on request).
2. No gate: any future RMSNorm backward call with a different signature or dtype layout reaches the Triton
   function directly.
